replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of data. It involves finding the directions of maximum variance in the data and projecting the data onto these directions. The first step is to standardize the data. Then, you compute the covariance matrix. Next, you find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. The eigenvectors are the principal components, and the eigenvalues represent the variance explained by each principal component. You can then sort the eigenvalues and select the top k eigenvalues to form a feature subspace. Finally, you project the original data onto this subspace to obtain the reduced data.
